Hi,

Yes, it's possible to load mirtCAT as any other R package in both 5.0 and 5.1.

In Concerto each test session will start separate R process. If you load mirtCAT, depending on available resources you have and your traffic, you can quickly run out of RAM, as loading mirtCAT package alone will eat up over 200MB above anything your R process already consumed.

From 5.1 you have an option to use R services. Basically it allows you to provision set amount of R processes (number is configurable), and offload some processing there. Requests coming there are queued and processed with 'first in, first out'. This is useful for heavy packages like mirtCAT, as you only load it in R service processes, so you know exactly how many processes will run with it loaded at any given point in time, making your whole application more scalable.

Best regards,
Przemyslaw Lis

On 06/07/2022 21:12, Vesselin Popov wrote:
Hi there, it's possible to load mirtcat like any other r package into concerto and use it. However since this is a super resource hungry package, it's only practically usable in the Dev branch, version 5.1, where there is an R service that lets you load hungry packages and call them without dealing with all of the knock on performance implications.

My colleague Przemek can give you more info on how to do this. Assuming of course that you actually can't do your bifactor model in catR...
